title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: On Monday a student tells your makerspace assistant that they use a wheelchair and need ground-floor machines. On Thursday, in a new session, the assistant asks them again. Which change makes the assistant remember this across sessions?

options.text: Switch to a model with a much larger context window
Save the fact in a note and load it each session
Keep chatting longer, since the model learns from talks
Turn on the built-in memory of the model's past sessions

items.stem: An agent run has three model calls. The system prompt plus tool descriptions is 800 tokens and the student's question is 200 tokens. After call 1 the model writes a 100-token tool request, and the tool returns 1,400 tokens. After call 2 the model writes another 100-token tool request, and that tool returns 600 tokens. Call 3 writes the final answer. Nothing is ever removed from the history. How many input tokens are sent to the model across the three calls in total?

Your assistant saved the note "Sam is trained on the laser cutter" six months ago. In one or two sentences, why is it risky to let the assistant approve a booking from that note alone, and what should it do instead?

Your search tool returns the chunk "Set the spindle to 12,000 rpm and the feed to 800 mm/min" for a question about the laser cutter, but the chunk comes from the CNC router manual. Which change to how the search index is built best prevents this?

options.text: Cut every chunk shorter so each holds fewer numbers
Return ten chunks per question instead of only three
Use a larger model to read each chunk once found
Put the machine, section and page in front of each chunk

items.stem: Your model's context window can hold a whole 96,000-token set of manuals. A teammate says, "Then we can put all the manuals in every call and stop managing context." Which reply is accurate?

options.text: It fits, but you pay for it on every call, and recall tends to get worse as the context fills
It works well, because the model reads every token in the window equally carefully, whatever the size
It works, because the manuals are stored inside the model after the very first call that sends them
It fails, because manuals must always be retrieved in pieces before any model call can use them
